findings.title: Circular import risk between incidents.grouptype and workflow_engine.processors.detector
findings.body: src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py now imports `StatefulDetectorHandler` from `sentry.workflow_engine.processors.detector`. That processor module imports `sentry.workflow_engine.models`, which in turn imports `sentry.issues.grouptype`. If the group-type registry (sentry.issues.grouptype) imports or is extended to import sentry.incidents.grouptype (as it does for other handler modules), this creates an import cycle: workflow_engine.processors.detector -> workflow_engine.models -> sentry.issues.grouptype -> sentry.incidents.grouptype -> workflow_engine.processors.detector. Depending on import order this will raise ImportError at startup or in first-request imports. The handler dependency should be inverted (e.g. lazy import or registration) to avoid coupling the issues/grouptype layer to the workflow_engine processor layer.

findings.title: Multi-group test builds expected occurrence for group_2 with wrong value (6 instead of 10)
findings.body: In test_state_results_multi_group, the data packet sets group_vals to {"group_1": 6, "group_2": 10}, but the expected occurrence for group_2 is built via `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(..., "group_2", 6, ...)` using value 6. The test only passes because the mock's build_occurrence_and_event_data ignores the `value` argument. This means the test does not actually verify that the correct per-group value is passed to build_occurrence_and_event_data; a bug that swapped values between group keys would go undetected. The mock should incorporate `value` into the occurrence (e.g. subtitle/evidence) so the assertion is meaningful.

findings.title: Removed duplicate-group-key coverage is not replaced
findings.body: The PR removes test_state_results_multi_group_dupe, which asserted behavior when the same group key appears twice. The rationale (dict keyed by group key) makes silent overwrite the new behavior, but there is no test asserting that a duplicate group key in the input results in exactly one produced occurrence rather than two. Since the old code explicitly logged an error and skipped duplicates, the new silent last-write-wins semantics (and the loss of the error signal) should be covered by a test to lock in the intended contract.
